scripts.text:
DECLARE @CurrentDate DATE = GETDATE() -- Replace with the actual file generation date if different
DECLARE @FileGeneratedDate DATE 
DECLARE @FirstParamStartDate DATE
DECLARE @FirstParamEndDate DATE

-- Set the third parameter to the current date (file generated date)
SET @FileGeneratedDate = @CurrentDate

DECLARE @BEGINDT DATE
DECLARE @ENDDT DATE

SET @BEGINDT =@0
SET @ENDDT = @1

IF (@BEGINDT = '1/1/1900' AND @ENDDT = '1/1/1900')
BEGIN
-- Helper variables to determine the 3rd Wednesday of the current month
			DECLARE @FirstDayOfMonth DATE = DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(@CurrentDate), MONTH(@CurrentDate), 1)
			DECLARE @WeekdayOfFirstDay INT = DATEPART(WEEKDAY, @FirstDayOfMonth)
			DECLARE @DaysToThirdWednesday INT

			-- Calculate the 3rd Wednesday of the month
			IF @WeekdayOfFirstDay <= 4 -- Check if the 1st of the month is before Wednesday
				SET @DaysToThirdWednesday = 3 - @WeekdayOfFirstDay + 1 + 14 -- Days till 3rd Wednesday
			ELSE
				SET @DaysToThirdWednesday = 10 - @WeekdayOfFirstDay + 14 -- Days till 3rd Wednesday if 1st is after Wednesday

			DECLARE @ThirdWednesdayOfMonth DATE = DATEADD(DAY, @DaysToThirdWednesday, @FirstDayOfMonth)

			-- Determine if the current date is before or after the 15th and the 3rd Wednesday
			IF DAY(@CurrentDate) < 15 AND @CurrentDate < @ThirdWednesdayOfMonth
			BEGIN
				-- If before the 15th and before the 3rd Wednesday, set to the first and last day of the month prior to the previous month
				SET @FirstParamStartDate = DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(DATEADD(MONTH, -2, @CurrentDate)), MONTH(DATEADD(MONTH, -2, @CurrentDate)), 1)
				SET @FirstParamEndDate = EOMONTH(DATEADD(MONTH, -2, @CurrentDate))
			END
			ELSE
			BEGIN
				-- If on or after the 15th or after the 3rd Wednesday, set to the first and last day of the previous month
				SET @FirstParamStartDate = DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(DATEADD(MONTH, -1, @CurrentDate)), MONTH(DATEADD(MONTH, -1, @CurrentDate)), 1)
				SET @FirstParamEndDate = EOMONTH(DATEADD(MONTH, -1, @CurrentDate))
			END
END

IF (@BEGINDT != '1/1/1900' OR @ENDDT != '1/1/1900') 
BEGIN
	SET @FirstParamStartDate = @BEGINDT
	SET @FirstParamEndDate = @ENDDT
END


-- Combine to form the filename
DECLARE @FileName NVARCHAR(100)
SET @FileName = 'Anthem_MemberContact_' + 
    FORMAT(@FirstParamStartDate, 'MMddyyyy') + '_' + 
    FORMAT(@FirstParamEndDate, 'MMddyyyy') + '_' + 
    FORMAT(@FileGeneratedDate, 'MMddyyyy') + '.txt'

-- Print the filename (or use it as needed)
SELECT @FileName AS [GeneratedFileName]
